summary: Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and held the Edmund J. and Louise W. Kahn Endowed Professorship at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2026).

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard (2003–2010) under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett. His career includes posts at Oberlin College (attested 2013) and the University of Miami (2013).
Justin Shimeld is a scholar in philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he was supervised by Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justin Václav Prášek (1853–1924) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Charles University (~1878–1882), studied at Munich and Berlin in 1885, and taught Édouard Huber.

Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1797 to 1801. He subsequently held a long-term position at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 until 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at Kiel (1823) and Königsberg (1853–1858).
Justyna Wiśniewska-Singh works in Indology and linguistics. She completed her MA and PhD at the University of Warsaw between 2001 and 2015, where she was appointed as Dr in 2016.

Jvala Singh specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia (2018–2024) and held an appointment as a lecturer at the University of California, Berkeley, in 2021.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was active in linguistics and other fields. His education included studies at Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864–1867).

János Harmatta (1917–2004) was a Hungarian scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. After earning his PhD at Eötvös Loránd University, he became professor there in 1952 and served as director at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

János Szerb (1951–1988) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD at Eötvös Loránd University (~1980–1982), he was a lecturer at the University of Vienna (1982) and a researcher at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1984–1988).

Jérôme Ducor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying under Jacques May and earning a D.Litt. from the University of Geneva, he served as curator at the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève (1995–2019) and taught at the universities of Lausanne and Geneva.

Józef Lączak (1926–1989) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helena Willman-Grabowska at Jagiellonian University. He lectured at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Warsaw, and the University of Helsinki, later heading the Indian Department at Jagiellonian University (1980–1989).

Józef Reczek (1936–1988) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Jagiellonian University (1953–1959) under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Tadeusz Pobożniak, and Tadeusz Milewski, becoming a docent there in 1972.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan, then served as professor and rector at Kazan State University (1833–1860) before joining the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939). He also taught Constantin Régamey.

József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, where he learned from Theodor Benfey. He worked at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and served as full professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).
József Schmidt (1868–1933) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1891–1899) under Aurel Mayr, whom he later succeeded, and served as docent there from 1908 to 1920.

Jörg B. Quenzer is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Hamburg (attested 2016–2026) and has served as an editor and editorial board member for Studies in Manuscript Cultures.

Jörg Heimbel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He has held positions at Hamburg, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.
